```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

# import necessary libraries
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(tidyr)
```

## RKI data on reported cases


```{r}
# Load data
may21 <- read_csv('/Users/inanb/Documents/GitHub/berlin_ode/2021-05-31_Deutschland_SarsCov2_Infektionen.csv')

# Filter for Berlin (IdLandkreis starts with "11")
berlin <- may21 %>%
  filter(startsWith(as.character(IdLandkreis), "11"))

# Group by date and sum over age groups
berlin_grouped <- berlin %>%
  group_by(Refdatum) %>%
  summarise(AnzahlFall = sum(AnzahlFall, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(Refdatum = as_date(Refdatum))
```

```{r}
# Create daily new cases dataframe
be <- berlin_grouped %>%
  rename(date = Refdatum, daily_new = AnzahlFall)

# Create complete date range and reindex, filling missing dates with 0
full_dates <- tibble(date = seq(min(be$date), max(be$date), by = "day"))

be <- full_dates %>%
  left_join(be, by = "date") %>%
  mutate(daily_new = replace_na(daily_new, 0))
```

```{r}
# Calculate active cases as current + previous 2 days
be <- be %>%
  mutate(active_cases = lead(daily_new, 2, default = 0) +
                       lead(daily_new, 1, default = 0) +
                       daily_new)

# Calculate cumulative and recovered
be <- be %>%
  mutate(cumulative_cases = cumsum(daily_new),
         recovered = lag(cumulative_cases, default = 0),
         susceptible = 3782202 - cumulative_cases)
```

```{r}
# First, gather the data to long format for plotting
plot_data <- be %>%
  select(date, daily_new, active_cases) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(daily_new, active_cases),
               names_to = "type", values_to = "count")

# Plot
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = date, y = count, color = type)) +
  geom_line(size = 1) +
  labs(title = "Daily New Cases and Active Cases in Berlin",
       x = "Date",
       y = "Number of Cases",
       color = "Type") +
  theme_minimal()

```



```{r}
# Normalize and build final berlin_data frame
berlin_data <- be %>%
  mutate(susceptible = susceptible / 3782202,
         infected = active_cases / 3782202,
         recovered = recovered / 3782202) %>%
  mutate(exposed = 0,
         symptomatic = 0,
         hospitalized = 0,
         critical = 0,
         deceased = 0,
         quarantine_S = 0,
         quarantine_E = 0,
         quarantine_I = 0,
         contact_traced = 0) %>%
  select(date, susceptible, exposed, infected, recovered, symptomatic,
         hospitalized, critical, deceased, quarantine_S, quarantine_E,
         quarantine_I, contact_traced) %>%
  arrange(date)
```
